content:
Apple today announced the first eight performances at its brand-new Apple Music Hall in London, kicking off with Elton John next week. Here are the details.

Elton John will headline the inaugural Apple Music Hall performance

Earlier this week, Apple revealed Apple Music Hall — a new concert venue at London's iconic Battersea Power Station, where Apple also has offices and a retail store.

Apple Music Hall will hold up to 600 people, with performances streamed globally via Apple Music. Performers will also receive finished Spatial Audio recordings, broadcast-quality mixes, and multi-camera video.

When Apple announced Apple Music Hall earlier, it said it would soon reveal the first artists to perform at the venue.

Apple confirmed the first eight performances today, with Elton John kicking things off next week. Here's the full lineup:

  • Elton John — September 28
  • Baby Keem — October 2
  • Skye Newman — October 7
  • Troye Sivan — October 13
  • Arlo Parks — October 22
  • Burna Boy — October 29
  • Chase & Status — November 26
  • Charli xcx — December 2

Some of the artists go way back with Apple Music. Elton John, for instance, has hosted his weekly radio show "Rocket Hour" on Apple Music since its launch in 2015; meanwhile, Charli xcx hosted her own show "The Candy Shop" on Beats 1 for five seasons.

As for the concerts, Apple says "Tickets for Elton John, Baby Keem, and Skye Newman will go on sale Monday, September 28 at 9 a.m. BST," and "tickets for all other shows will go on sale at a later date."

For more ticketing and show information, click here.

Apple Music requires a valid subscription. Users can sign up for $11.99 per month, with the first month free, or subscribe as part of an Apple One bundle.
